title: Seafood Paella
subtitle: Spanish saffron rice with seafood
excerpt: The Valencian one-pan rice dish: short-grain rice cooked in a wide, flat pan with saffron-infused stock, seafood, and aromatics until the grains are just cooked and a golden, caramelised crust has formed on the bottom of the pan. The crust is the point.

recipe.sourceNotes: Paella originates from the Valencia region of Spain, where it was historically a midday meal cooked by agricultural workers over wood fires in a wide, flat iron pan called a paellera. The original Valencian paella used rabbit, chicken, and green beans; the seafood version is a later development associated with coastal areas. The defining feature is the socarrat, the toasted, caramelised layer of rice that forms on the bottom of the pan when the liquid has evaporated and the heat continues. Achieving the socarrat without burning the rice requires experience and attention. The rice should never be stirred once the stock is added; paella is not risotto. Short-grain Bomba rice from Valencia is the traditional choice and absorbs up to three times its volume in stock without breaking apart.

content.text: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added. The crust on the bottom forms by staying in contact with the heat, not by moving. Use a wide, flat pan; the rice should be no more than 2 cm deep so it cooks evenly. The stock must be well seasoned and very hot when it goes in.

Heat the olive oil in a large, wide pan or paella pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and paprika. Cook for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick.

Add the squid and cook for 2 minutes. Add the rice and stir to coat in the tomato mixture for 1 minute. Pour in the hot stock and the saffron with its soaking water. Season. Arrange the prawns and mussels across the top. Do not stir.

Cook over medium-high heat for 15 minutes without stirring until the stock has been absorbed. Listen for a crackling sound from the bottom of the pan; this is the socarrat forming. Cook for 1 to 2 more minutes, then remove from the heat. Cover with foil and rest for 5 minutes. Serve scattered with parsley with lemon wedges alongside.
